verdict_reasoning: The bug is real and reproducible (messages #1 and #2), and no surviving objection is against fixing it. The open points are fixable design questions about v3: replication-ondisk-1 (summarized deleter), standards-compat-1 (false positives on back branches), replication-ondisk-2 (reset of the global variable) and standards-compat-2 (exclusion constraints). v3 has no review, and its commit message and files are not shown, so these need a committer who knows predicate.c.

brief.title: Detect SSI conflicts when unique checks rely on a committed delete
brief.problem: A serializable transaction can read a row, insert a new row with the same primary key because another transaction deleted the old one, see both rows, and commit. Unique checks use SnapshotDirty, which does not take part in SSI. The bug fires only when the deleter used a secondary index, and it also affects INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING.
brief.proposed_design: v1 has the table AM report the deleting XID when SnapshotDirty skips a tuple still visible to the transaction snapshot. SSI then fails only if an rw-conflict to that transaction already exists, and flags the transaction for abort so a savepoint rollback cannot hide the error. v3, by another author, avoids an ABI change: it checks the key against the transaction's own snapshot and uses a per-backend global variable.
user_visible_surface: New serialization failures on inserts and ON CONFLICT that reuse a key freed by a concurrent serializable delete.
v1 adds a new table AM callback in tableam.h, which out-of-tree table AMs must provide.
author_claims: The window is narrow but plausible in delete-and-recreate or upsert workflows with long transactions.
The bug does not corrupt the index or leave a lasting duplicate, but it breaks the SERIALIZABLE guarantee.
v1 avoids a false positive when the rw-conflict is to an unrelated transaction.
v3 keeps the ABI and existing behaviour, so it can be backpatched.
An earlier Alekseev PoC caused a false positive that broke partition-key-update-3.spec; v2 and later claim to avoid it.
brief.thread_state: Borodin posted v1, and Bryan Green reported several holes in it; Alekseev then took over with an ABI-preserving approach, ending with v3 and a commit message. Nobody has reviewed v3, and nobody has said whether it covers Green's cases.
unclear: The v3 commit message and touched files are not shown, so its design is known only from Alekseev's mail.
No reply says whether v3 handles deferred constraints, a summarized deleter, the DDL false positive, and exclusion constraints.
Nobody has decided whether exclusion constraints are in scope or a follow-up.
No one has measured the cost of the extra snapshot check on unique inserts.
No reply says which back branches v3 targets.

objections.title: Conflict check loses the deleter once it is summarized
objections.failure_scenario: A busy serializable workload forces SummarizeOldestCommittedSxact to move the committed deleter into the old-committed summary. Session 1 then reuses the freed key and commits with both rows visible. Nobody notices, because the anomaly appears only under load and leaves no error.
objections.argument: Message #3 showed that v1 looks up the deleter's sxact, gets NULL after summarization, and returns without failing. Summarization keeps only coarse conflict data, so a check for an rw-conflict to that exact transaction cannot work once the deleter is summarized. The fix then depends on how much other serializable traffic runs at the same time. Messages #4 to #7 describe v3 without saying whether it relies on the deleter's sxact or how it acts after summarization.
objections.author_must_show: When the deleting transaction has already been summarized, does v3 fail conservatively, and which isolation test forces summarization to prove it?

critic.reasoning: v3 asks the transaction's own snapshot, so it may not need the deleter's sxact at all. Messages #4 to #7 do not say so, and Green's summarization case has no reply and no stated test.

objections.title: Back-branch fix adds new serialization failures with unproven false-positive scope
objections.failure_scenario: A minor release ships v3 to a stable branch. A serializable application that drops and re-creates a catalog object, or reuses a key freed by an unrelated transaction, starts getting SQLSTATE 40001 on statements that committed before. If its retry loop does not cover DDL, the deploy job fails after a routine minor upgrade.
objections.argument: v3 is presented as backpatchable because it keeps the ABI and "existing behaviour" (message #6), but it adds new errors by design. Message #3 showed v1 rejecting valid CREATE TABLE after a concurrent DROP, and message #5 showed an earlier PoC breaking partition-key-update-3.spec. No reply says whether v3 avoids the DDL case or limits the recheck to relations that need predicate locking. Back branches tolerate new errors only for real anomalies.
objections.author_must_show: Which existing isolation specs and Green's DDL history pass unchanged under v3, and which back branches is it meant for?

critic.reasoning: Message #6 claims v2 keeps existing behaviour, which plausibly covers partition-key-update-3.spec. No message says v3 gates the check on relations that need predicate locking, so Green's DROP TABLE / CREATE TABLE history stays open for a back-branch fix.

objections.title: Per-backend global in v3 has no stated reset on error
objections.failure_scenario: A unique check sets the per-backend variable, then an ERROR or a savepoint rollback interrupts the insert before the variable is cleared. The next insert in that backend reads the stale value. It either raises a serialization failure that should not happen or skips one it needs, and the user sees no cause.
objections.argument: Message #6 says v3 adds a per-backend global variable so it can avoid an ABI change, and plans to refactor it later on master. The thread does not say where the variable is set, where it is cleared, or whether transaction abort and subtransaction abort reset it. A back-branch fix built on global state needs that pairing written down, because back branches are hard to change after release.
objections.author_must_show: Where is the v3 global variable reset on transaction abort, subtransaction abort and ERROR inside the unique check, and which test covers a savepoint rollback?

critic.reasoning: Message #6 confirms the per-backend global variable and gives no set or reset points. The stale-value scenario cannot be ruled out without the code, and v1 already had to treat savepoint rollback specially.

objections.title: Unique and exclusion constraints would give different serializable guarantees
objections.failure_scenario: A user replaces a primary key with EXCLUDE USING btree (k WITH =), or uses a range exclusion constraint for bookings. The same delete-then-reuse history that now fails under a unique index still commits a duplicate under the exclusion constraint. The user finds out only when the data shows two conflicting rows.
objections.argument: Message #3 reproduced the anomaly with an exclusion constraint, which runs its own dirty-snapshot scan outside _bt_check_unique. The v1 commit message states a root cause that covers both paths, but the fix touches only nbtree. Nobody in the thread has said whether exclusion constraints are in scope or a documented follow-up. Fixing one path and backpatching it would leave SERIALIZABLE behaviour depending on the constraint type, with no note to users.
objections.author_must_show: Does v3 cover the exclusion-constraint path, and if not, where is the remaining gap recorded for users?

critic.reasoning: Message #3 says the gap predates the patch and that fcff8a57519 was also nbtree-only, so a follow-up is acceptable. The objection asks only for a scope statement, and no later message gives one.

objections.title: No SSI-qualified reviewer has looked at the version proposed for commit
objections.failure_scenario: A committer backpatches v3 to all supported branches based only on its own tests. Message #3 lists cases that v3 might still miss: deferred constraints, a summarized deleter, DDL false positives and exclusion constraints. A user then hits one of them after a minor release, with no SSI expert engaged to fix it.
objections.argument: Bryan Green reviewed v1 only (message #3). Messages #5 to #7 change the design twice, and nobody has replied to any of them. SSI is an area few committers know well, and a backpatched change there ties every supported branch to this design.
objections.author_must_show: Which of the cases from message #3 does v3 cover, and has a committer familiar with predicate.c agreed to review it for backpatching?

critic.reasoning: The CommitFest entry lists one reviewer, who saw only v1, and messages #5 to #7 have no replies. This belongs in the committability field and must not raise the verdict on the idea.

refuted.title: Back-branch fix relies on a per-backend global with no stated lifecycle
refuted.failure_scenario: A unique check sets the per-backend variable, then an error or a savepoint rollback interrupts it before the value is consumed. The next unique check in the same backend reads the stale value and raises a false serialization failure, or skips a real one. Nobody notices until a user reports a failure that is hard to reproduce.
refuted.argument: Message #6 says v3 adds a per-backend global variable and calls it "not pretty", but the visible material does not say where it is set, read and reset, or how it behaves across errors. Hidden state shared between nbtree and SSI is the kind of coupling that later patches miss without anything failing loudly. Message #6 also plans to refactor master after the backpatch, so master and the back branches would carry different SSI code for years.
refuted.author_must_show: Where is the v3 global set, consumed and reset, including on error and subtransaction abort, and does master take the same design or a different one?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of replication-ondisk-2. Its one added point, different code on master and back branches, is common practice for ABI-preserving back-branch fixes and has no failure scenario of its own.

refuted.title: No statement that the new check costs nothing outside serializable
refuted.failure_scenario: An OLTP workload at read committed does many unique inserts into a table with frequent deletes. If the extra snapshot check in v3 runs on every unique insert that meets a dead tuple, these users pay for an SSI fix they do not need, and the cost shows up only after a minor release.
refuted.argument: Message #4 describes v3 as asking the transaction's own snapshot the same question that the dirty-snapshot check answers. Neither message #6 nor message #7 says whether this check runs only for serializable transactions on relations that need predicate locking, and no measurement is shown. A minor release is a poor place to find a regression on unique inserts.
refuted.author_must_show: Is the v3 check skipped entirely unless the transaction is serializable and the relation needs predicate locking, and what does a unique-insert benchmark show?

critic.reasoning: The scenario depends on v3 lacking a serializable gate, which the proposal does not suggest. Even ungated, the check runs only when a unique insert finds an equal-key tuple that SnapshotDirty skips, a path that already does a heap fetch.

touch_points.label: ABI / extension API
touch_points.reason: v1 adds a table AM callback in tableam.h; v3 avoids it with a per-backend global variable.

touch_points.label: SQL-standard conflict or non-standard syntax
touch_points.reason: see objection standards-compat-1: Back-branch fix adds new serialization failures with unproven false-positive scope

touch_points.label: backpatchability
touch_points.reason: v3 is meant for back branches and adds new serialization failures there.

touch_points.label: maintenance burden ("who maintains this in 10 years")
touch_points.reason: The fix couples nbtree unique checks to predicate.c, and master may later differ from the back branches.

touch_points.label: performance on the hot path
touch_points.reason: The change adds a check in the nbtree unique-check path in nbtinsert.c; nobody has measured it.

touch_points.label: doesn't fit what Postgres is about (extension / external tool / already solved)

questions: When the deleting transaction has already been summarized, does v3 still raise a serialization failure, and which isolation test forces summarization?
Does v3 skip the check on relations that do not need predicate locking, so Green's DROP TABLE / CREATE TABLE history from message #3 still commits?
Does v3 catch the deferred-constraint history from message #3, where the recheck runs as UNIQUE_CHECK_EXISTING?
Where is the v3 per-backend global variable reset on ERROR, transaction abort and subtransaction abort?
Are exclusion constraints in scope for this patch or a follow-up, and which back branches does v3 target?

committability.owner_note: It needs a committer who knows SSI (predicate.c) and nbtree unique checks; none has spoken in the visible thread.
committability.liability: The owner signs for new serialization failures in every back branch that gets the fix, including any false positives, and for SSI code that differs between master and back branches if master is refactored later.
committability.author_follow_up: Alekseev took over from v1 and posted through v3 with a commit message, and the CommitFest entry lists both authors; no reply to Green's cases is visible.

priority.reason: The fix restores the SERIALIZABLE guarantee for users of that isolation level, and the window is narrow. v3 is unreviewed and no SSI-qualified committer is engaged; review cost is a guess because the v3 patch was not read.

provisional_note: The v3 commit message, touched files and code are not shown, so its design is known only from the brief. Whether it already covers the cases in message #3 could not be checked.

precedents_retrieved.title: SERIALIZABLE on standby servers
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch allows SERIALIZABLE READ ONLY DEFERRABLE transactions on standby servers by having the primary write snapshot safety information into commit records and separate WAL records. The standby waits for a point in the WAL stream where a snapshot is known to be safe, using hypothetical transactions that the primary tracks as stand-ins for standby transactions.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The author called the patch prototype/WIP code with unsolved problems. Two of them are a race between the safety decision and the order of commit records in WAL, and the absence of snapshot safety information in checkpoints. A third is that the primary makes transactions visible in ProcArrayEndTransaction() order while the standby uses commit record order, which can allow serialization anomalies. No review of the general approach came, and the entry was later withdrawn; the visible messages do not show who withdrew it.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: And that's precisely the issue: on the primary, transactions become visible to other transactions in the order in which they perform ProcArrayEndTransaction(), but on the standby, they become visible in the order in which they RecordTransactionCommit().

precedents_retrieved.title: WIP: Pgbench Errors and serialization/deadlock retries
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch lets pgbench clients keep running after serialization and deadlock failures instead of disconnecting, and reports these failures in progress output, logs and final reports. Later versions roll back and retry the failed script up to a configurable maximum number of tries.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The visible messages do not show why. The last messages shown are a partial review by Fabien COELHO in August 2017 listing many open points, then a December 2017 reply from the author on some of them; the messages before the March 2018 decision are not shown.

precedents_retrieved.title: WIP: Pgbench Errors and serialization/deadlock retries
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch lets pgbench clients survive serialization and deadlock failures instead of disconnecting, retry the failed script as a transaction (controlled by --max-tries and --latency-limit), and report failures and retries in progress output, logs and the final report. Later versions split out preparatory patches for a RandomState structure, a Variables structure and a new error reporting function.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Michael Paquier returned the patch with feedback because Fabien COELHO's last reviews had stayed unanswered for a couple of weeks. The main open objection was that the v11 main patch also changed behavior for meta-command and other SQL errors: pgbench counted them as failures and kept looping instead of aborting with a clear message. Fabien asked that this change be removed and proposed separately. Smaller code and naming issues from his reviews were also still open.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: I'm mostly saying that your patch should focus on implementing the retry feature when appropriate, and avoid changing the behavior (error displayed, abort or not) on features unrelated to serialization & deadlock errors.

precedents_retrieved.title: Fix race condition in SSI when reading PredXact->SxactGlobalXmin
precedents_retrieved.summary: DropAllPredicateLocksFromTable, PredicateLockPageSplit and CheckTableForSerializableConflictIn read PredXact->SxactGlobalXmin without a lock and can see InvalidTransactionId while SetNewSxactGlobalXmin recomputes it, then skip needed SIRead lock work. The attached patch takes SerializableXactHashLock for these reads; the author also described an alternative where SetNewSxactGlobalXmin assigns the new xmin only after the scan.
precedents_retrieved.objection: No one objected to the fix. The entry was withdrawn the day the author pointed out that two commitfest entries existed for the same patch (6037, his own, and 6145, registered by Mihail Nikalayeu), so it was probably closed as a duplicate. The visible messages do not say which entry was withdrawn. A .spec reproducer with injection points was requested and still pending.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
I guess one of the commitfest entries should be deleted? I had already made
one already.

precedents_retrieved.title: Statement-level Triggers For Uniqueness Checks
precedents_retrieved.summary: Replace the per-row constraint triggers that recheck deferrable unique and primary key constraints with one insert and one update statement-level trigger per constraint. unique_key_recheck() would walk the transition table, so large inserts and updates fire fewer triggers and lock the unique index fewer times.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The author withdrew the entry after a proof-of-concept patch whose triggers did not fire. Dean Rasheed showed that the existing row-level path queues a recheck only for rows that index insertion flags as possible conflicts, so bulk inserts often queue no rechecks at all. The author then judged the possible gain smaller than first thought. Peter Eisentraut replied that the recheckIndexes logic could be adapted to statement triggers, and the visible thread has no further reply from the author.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
Dean's information made me
think the potential for a gain is smaller than initially imagined.

precedents_retrieved.title: Improve amcheck to check UNIQUE constraint in btree index
precedents_retrieved.objectors: Peter Geoghegan, Mark Dilger, David Steele
precedents_retrieved.summary: Extend contrib/amcheck's bt_index_check and bt_index_parent_check so that, for btree indexes with a UNIQUE constraint, they detect duplicate keys whose heap tuples are visible, including duplicates spanning adjacent leaf pages, and report the index and heap TIDs involved. Later versions added an optional argument to enable the uniqueness check and a regression test variant for 32-bit systems.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Reviewers asked for further changes: Peter Geoghegan objected to reporting violations as WARNINGs, to the message saying an index only might be corrupt (calling it an unacceptable false positive), to the handling of cross-page duplicates, and to tests that update pg_index, and suggested opclass-based fault injection and sharing the heapallindexed snapshot. Mark Dilger's review of v4 asked for documentation updates, pg_amcheck integration with TAP tests, and a different test approach. No updated patch followed for several weeks, and David Steele marked it Returned with Feedback because it needed more work and had not been updated.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
This patch appears to need some work and has not been updated in several
weeks, so marking Returned with Feedback.

precedents_retrieved.title: Allow self-conflicting INSERT INTO .. ON CONFLICT DO UPDATEs
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch lets INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE accept a command whose own proposed rows conflict with each other, as DO NOTHING already does. Today such a command fails with "command cannot affect row a second time".
precedents_retrieved.objection: Andres Freund and Peter Geoghegan voted against it, and the CFM returned it citing those two votes. Andres Freund objected that the patch makes one command update a row it inserted, producing cmin == cmax and breaking heap visibility rules. The author then found visibility bugs in his own patch. Peter Geoghegan argued that updating the same row twice in one command is not desirable and asked who would want it.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: To me it seems as if allowing the same command to update the same row more than once is just not desirable in general.

precedents_retrieved.title: conflict handling for COPY FROM
precedents_retrieved.objectors: Andres Freund, Andrew Dunstan, Alvaro Herrera
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch lets COPY FROM skip rows that fail with unique or exclusion constraint violations, and later some format errors, up to an error limit set by a GUC or option. Failed rows go to a log file named in the command so the user can examine them.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Andres Freund objected that writing a server-side log file requires superuser rights, unlike COPY from STDIN. Andrew Dunstan and Andres suggested logging failed rows to a table or returning them as rows instead. Andres marked the entry returned with feedback after the author did not answer these comments for weeks. The author's later version reported skipped rows as warnings, which Alvaro Herrera called useless for this purpose; he supported returning rows.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: Again, that requires super user permissions (in contrast to copy from/to stdin/out).

roaster_notes.note: No precedent found: the precedent list has no earlier rejected, returned or reverted attempt at this idea. Messages #1 and #2 point only to fcff8a57519 and a related ON CONFLICT thread as related work, and neither is reported as a rejection.
The proposal adds no syntax, GUC, catalog object or pg_dump state. New serialization failures for real anomalies follow the SERIALIZABLE contract and are not a compatibility objection in themselves.
There is no on-disk format, WAL, catalog, wire protocol or pg_upgrade change, and v3 drops the v1 table AM callback. The nbtree VACUUM bookkeeping invariant does not apply here.

The proposal has no privilege or exposure aspect. It adds serialization failures only where a transaction's own snapshot still sees the key, so it reveals no more than unique checks and SSI errors already do. Bryan Green reviewed v1 for security in message #3 and raised only non-security points, and no one has reviewed v3 the same way.
The goal is a real SERIALIZABLE correctness bug and belongs in core. These objections concern the shape of v3 and who will own it, not whether to fix the bug.

This is a correctness fix for SERIALIZABLE, and no existing feature, setting or extension restores the guarantee for unique checks that rely on a committed delete. Explicit row locks in application code avoid only some cases and do not fix the isolation level, so this angle has nothing to raise.

This is a correctness fix for a documented guarantee, so lack of user demand does not apply. Message #1 gives a reproducible SERIALIZABLE anomaly, and Message #2 confirms it, including the ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING case. Users who choose SERIALIZABLE rely on that guarantee without asking for it, and the new serialization failures land only on serializable transactions that hit the anomaly. Whether v3 covers the cases in Message #3 is a design question for other angles.
